name: West Ridge / Colonial Glacier

pitch_detail.notes: Pyramid Lake Trail to Pyramid Ridge to high camp (~5,400-6,100 ft), partly off-trail.
Roped travel across the Colonial Glacier, crevasse hazard present.
Exposed running-belay snow traverse beneath cornices, moving from the NW to NE side of the peak; steep snow up to ~30 degrees.
Short, occasionally loose rock scramble along the west ridge to the summit.

rappel_detail.notes: Optional short single-rope rappel that some parties use; the descent is otherwise a downclimb.
rappel_detail.anchor: existing sling or webbing around a rock horn, not bolted; inspect it
rappel_detail.station: On the Class 3-4 rock near the summit ridge.

rappels: 1 optional short single-rope rappel from a slung horn near the summit ridge; otherwise a downclimb
descent_text: Reverse the ascent line: downclimb the east ridge back to the head of the Northeast Gully, then downclimb/plunge-step the snow gully back down to the Colonial-Snowfield col, drop back onto the Colonial Glacier, and retrace the rope-up glacier traverse and the loose scree/boulder traverse beneath Pyramid Peak back to the Pyramid Ridge camp, then follow the climbers' path and maintained Pyramid Lake Trail back to the car. This is fundamentally a walk-off/downclimb, not a rappel-dependent descent — but on the class 3-4 rock near the summit ridge, trip reports document an existing rap station (a sling/webbing anchor around a rock horn, not bolted) that some parties use for a short single-rope rappel (roughly 20-30m, any single rope 30m+ works) over the steepest step; other parties simply downclimb this same section instead, since it's optional class 3-4 terrain for a confident scrambler. There is no other fixed or bolted rappel infrastructure reported on this route. Descent hazards mirror the approach in reverse: softening glacier snow and weaker crevasse bridges later in the day, loose rock in the gully and on the summit ridge scramble, potential rockfall on the Pyramid traverse, and the reported cornice hazard along the glacier traverse near the col — parties should time the glacier/col crossing for firm early-morning or evening snow rather than midday.
approach: Start at the signed Pyramid Lake Trailhead on SR 20 (small pullout on the north side of the highway, ~21 miles east of Marblemount and just past the Diablo turnoff, elev. ~1,150 ft; no parking pass needed, NPS backcountry permit if camping). Follow the maintained Pyramid Lake Trail — a well-used boot path through second-growth and old-growth forest — which climbs a steady, unrelenting ~1,500-1,600 ft over about 2.1-2.3 miles to Pyramid Lake (~2,600 ft). This maintained-trail portion ends at the lake; everything above is climbers'-trail/off-trail travel. Pick up the boot path around the right (east/north) side of the lake and continue climbing, now through brush, heather, and talus, gaining roughly 2,000 more feet up onto the crest of Pyramid Ridge. A knoll around 5,400-5,500 ft on this ridge is the customary high camp/bivy — seasonal ponds and puddles here and near ~4,500 ft (reported dry by late summer in low-snow years) are the last reliable water before the glacier. From the ridge crest, follow the climbers' path along the ridge over several knolls toward the base of Pyramid Peak, then drop and traverse a mix of scree and boulder-hop terrain beneath Pyramid's crumbly north face to reach the flat 6,100 ft basin at the toe of the Colonial Glacier — this traverse is loose underfoot and exposed to rockfall from above, and is the route's main approach-specific hazard. From the glacier-toe basin, rope up for glacier travel and ascend the Colonial Glacier, trending southeast/east across the upper glacier (crevasses are usually well-bridged under seasonal snow but are present and have been reported as a hazard, along with cornices along the traverse toward the Colonial-Snowfield col that are invisible from camp below) to reach the Colonial-Snowfield col or the base of the historic Northeast Gully. From the col, leave the ice for a loose gully leading up onto the West Ridge, which is then followed via Class 3-4 rock scrambling to the summit horn. Total car-to-summit distance runs roughly 10-14 miles round trip (parties differ depending on camp placement) with the ~6,600 ft of gain split roughly evenly between the maintained trail, the ridge/scree traverse, and the glacier-to-summit push.
overview: Colonial Peak is one of the steepest-rising summits in the North Cascades, gaining roughly 6,500+ ft above Diablo Lake's Thunder Arm in under 2.5 horizontal miles. It lies in the North Unit of North Cascades National Park, accessed through the Ross Lake National Recreation Area corridor along SR 20, and shares its glaciated basin with Snowfield Peak, Neve Peak, and Paul Bunyan's Stump — a popular multi-summit basin for Mountaineers-style basic glacier climbs. The standard route (sometimes called the West Ridge) climbs the Colonial Glacier on the northeast side to the Colonial-Snowfield col, then follows the ridge over talus and firn to a short, exposed class 3-4 summit block. First climbed July 31, 1931 by William Degenhardt and Herbert Strandberg.
beta: West Ridge via the Colonial Glacier. From the Pyramid Lake Trailhead on SR-20, follow the trail to Pyramid Lake, then a steep climbers' path up the forested rib to camps near the edge of the Colonial Glacier (~6,000 ft). Cross the glacier toward the Colonial-Snowfield col, gain the west ridge through a notch, and follow the exposed ridge (class 3-4 with short low-5th steps) to the summit; many parties rappel the summit block on descent. Crevasse hazard on the glacier; loose rock and exposure on the ridge. Ice axe, crampons, rope, and glacier kit required. Best July-September. No confirmed public GPS track for this route; navigation skills required.
gear: Ice axe and crampons for the glacier approach and the snow finger below the summit ridge
Rope and 2-3 pickets for the Colonial Glacier crossing — crevasses open by mid-summer
Helmet for the rock ridge finish
Sturdy boots; the last stretch to the summit is exposed 3rd/4th-class scrambling on rock, not technical climbing — no rack needed
A backcountry camping permit if overnighting near Pyramid Lake/Colonial Glacier
fa: William Degenhardt & Herbert Strandberg (Seattle Mountaineers), July 31, 1931 — this is the peak's first-ascent party and also the standard/easiest route line
face: West Ridge (Colonial Glacier side); final class 3 section on the north-facing upper slopes
